topic: First Formula One World Championship race: British Grand Prix (Grand Prix d'Europe), Silverstone, 13 May 1950, on a circuit laid out on the runways and perimeter track of RAF Silverstone, a wartime Wellington bomber training base; attended by King George VI and Queen Elizabeth; won by Giuseppe Farina (Alfa Romeo 158), who clinched the first drivers' title at the Italian Grand Prix, Monza, 3 September 1950; the 1950 season had 7 rounds (incl. Indianapolis 500); the 2026 calendar has 24 rounds, finishing in Abu Dhabi in December.
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: Formula 1 began at Monza or Monaco, the sport's oldest famous circuits.
myths.reality: Monaco (1929) and Monza (1922) hosted Grands Prix long before the championship, but the first World Championship round was Silverstone on 13 May 1950.

f1_1950.title: 1950 British Grand Prix — race result and report

silverstone_history.title: The history of Silverstone
silverstone_history.notes: RAF Silverstone opened 1943 as a Wellington bomber training base; the circuit used its runways and perimeter roads; hosted the first round of the F1 World Championship on 13 May 1950 before King George VI and Queen Elizabeth

britannica_farina.title: Giuseppe Farina — Italian racing driver
britannica_farina.notes: won the first World Championship Grand Prix at Silverstone in 1950 and became the first world champion, clinching the title at Monza

motorsport_1950.title: 1950 British Grand Prix race report
motorsport_1950.notes: Alfa Romeo 158s finished 1-2-3, Farina from Fagioli and Parnell; royal family present; 7-round championship
